content_of_post_to_comment:
When I travel abroad, its like I can easily stay consistent with good habits, but when i come back home i'm always hit with a sense of monotony and post-travel depression that makes it hard for any discipline to stick. My current environment is so boring to me and it's the same place I've failed so many times so it's like my brain associates failure and inaction with where I live.

So i was wondering, what advice would you give to someone who's tired of their environment, more specifically the way their house looks and feels, and in the future when I move abroad, how would I keep things interesting in my daily life when I'm coming back home to the same place my brain associates negative emotions with? I'm definitely missing some deeper context here for why I find it hard to get anything done in my house, and the contrast is insane when I juxtapose that with how much stuff I get done in another country, or even just another person's house in my country.
comment: I wonder if the travel effect is less about the country itself and more about your environment not carrying your old identity. At home, every corner might remind you of unfinished goals, while abroad you have no history attached to you. Maybe try changing one room or creating a few "away from home" routines there so your brain gets new cues instead of the same old ones.
